messages:
sam.r: Heads-up: ran into a flaky failure in our Kotlin SDK when Retrofit suspend calls are cancelled due to a coroutine timeout. Sometimes the library retries the HTTP request and we end up with duplicate side-effects. Repro notes below.

sam.r: Repro environment: Pixel 4 emulator Android 11, okhttp 4.10.0, retrofit 2.9 with suspend endpoints, using callTimeout(10_000) and readTimeout(5_000). Background: we wrap retrofit service calls in withTimeout to enforce higher-level deadlines.

sam.r: Code: 
```
suspend fun upload(data: RequestBody) {
  withTimeout(8_000) {
    api.upload(data) // suspend Retrofit call
  }
}
```

sam.r: Observed: when withTimeout fires it cancels coroutine, and okhttp cancels the Call. But occasionally okhttp keeps a queued/h2 stream and the server receives the body and processes it; then okhttp retry logic replays the request on another stream -> duplicate upload.

lina.v: Interesting. Are you using HTTP/2 multiplexing? H2 can keep streams in-flight and server might process late-arriving body. Also, Retrofit suspend functions use Call.await under the hood and cancellation translates to Call.cancel(). That doesn't guarantee server-side abort.

bilal.s: Two things to check: (1) callTimeout vs readTimeout semantics — callTimeout cancels the whole call after the timeout, while readTimeout only affects socket read. (2) If request body is streaming (not repeatable), a retry will fail unless OkHttp buffers it or you provide a replayable RequestBody.

sam.r: We're using streaming RequestBody for >10MB uploads to avoid memory spikes. I think when coroutine cancels, the socket close races with server read. Sometimes server finishes and returns 200 while client already threw TimeoutCancellationException. Then our client code retries at a higher layer (we have an outer retry policy) because we saw a cancellation and assumed failure.

lina.v: That outer retry is the smoking gun. If cancellation happened but server actually succeeded, retry leads to duplicate. Two approaches: (A) make retry decision based on okhttp response (if any) rather than only on coroutine exception, or (B) make uploads idempotent (use uploadId + server-side dedupe) or (C) buffer small bodies so OkHttp can reliably know eventual success/failure.

bilal.s: Also check dispatcher starvation: if you use Dispatchers.IO with too many blocking operations, coroutine cancellations don't always propagate timely. That can create weird race windows.

sam.r: Good call. We do some blocking crypto on the same thread pool before the suspend call. I'll move crypto to a single-threaded executor or use withContext(Dispatchers.Default) to avoid blocking IO dispatcher.

lina.v: Quick config suggestions: 
- set callTimeout on OkHttp to slightly higher than your withTimeout so OkHttp is the source of truth for total call lifetime.
- or wrap only network IO in withTimeout to avoid cancelling the whole call during pre/post processing.

sam.r: Example change we tried: 
```
okHttpClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .callTimeout(9_000, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(false) // don't replay streaming bodies automatically
  .build()
```

sam.r: After setting retryOnConnectionFailure(false) duplicates dropped in our smoke runs. However, we still want safe defaults in the SDK.

bilal.s: For SDK: defaulting retryOnConnectionFailure to false for clients that include streaming upload helpers might be sensible. Add docs: "suspend function cancellation may not reflect server result; avoid blind retries for non-idempotent calls."

lina.v: Also add a note on HTTP/2: multiplexed streams can complete on the server side after client cancel; client cannot assume server aborted on cancel. Recommend server-side idempotency token for uploads where duplicates are harmful.

qa-bot: test-run 2132104600 completed: api-upload-smoke (sam.r) -> flaky(2/10) initial, 0/10 after disabling retryOnConnectionFailure.

sam.r: Thanks QA. Action items: 
- update SDK docs with a section "Cancellations, timeouts, and retries" (small how-to).
- change default client in android sample to disable automatic retries for streaming uploads and show a buffered RequestBody helper.
- add example of using unique uploadId header for server-side dedupe.

bilal.s: I'll open a PR for the docs + sample and a small helper class for a replayable buffered RequestBody (with clear warning about memory). Keep default unchanged for simple clients but sample shows recommended pattern.

sam.r: Perfect. Leaving the thread open while we iterate on PR. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:
